evals.prompt: Scrivi il testo per la vetrina di un panificio di quartiere che apre il 3 dicembre in via del Pratello a Bologna. Si chiama Forno Nero, fa pane a lievitazione naturale e apre alle 7. Massimo 60 parole.
evals.expected_output: An Italian window sign that communicates the opening at a glance within the word limit.
assertions: The reply is in Italian and the sign is at most 60 words.
The sign conveys Forno Nero, via del Pratello in Bologna, 3 December, the 7 o’clock opening and natural leavening.
A detail such as the hour or the leavening shapes what the reader imagines beyond the address and opening information.
The sign makes no unsupported claims about the street, its residents or the business.

evals.prompt: can you make this less generic? it's the hero of our landing page for a shared shopping-list app for flatmates: "Empower your household with seamless collaboration. Organize, share and simplify your life."
evals.expected_output: An English headline and subline grounded in a recognizable shared-flat situation.
assertions: The reply leads with usable hero copy.
The scene makes the purpose of a shared shopping list intelligible and replaces the abstract benefits in the source.
The copy claims no feature beyond the shared list.

evals.prompt: Make the message our banking app shows when a bank transfer fails more creative. Right now it says: "Error 402. Operation failed."
evals.expected_output: A short failed-transfer message with the original identifier and clearly marked fields for the unresolved customer questions.
assertions: The message identifies the failed transfer and preserves code 402.
The message reserves a field for the verified debit status and a field for a verified next step.
The message promises no account state, refund time, safe retry, available control or support channel that the brief did not establish.
Any instructions for the team to fill in the fields appear separately from customer copy.

evals.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post announcing that our logistics company, Ferrando Transport, has achieved ISO 14001 certification. Brand guidelines: institutional tone, no emoji, no exclamation marks, 120 words maximum. Make it a bit less boring than usual.
evals.expected_output: An institutional post announcing the supplied certification, with a deliberate opening and no invented supporting claims.
assertions: The post names Ferrando Transport and ISO 14001, uses no emoji or exclamation marks, and stays within 120 words.
Its opening conveys the news without a stock expression of pride.
The post preserves an institutional voice without adding unverified certifiers, dates, emissions reductions or operational practices.

evals.prompt: dame tres ideas fuera de lo común para el vídeo de lanzamiento de nuestro helado de sésamo negro
evals.expected_output: Three distinct Spanish launch-video concepts with an observable action and a role for the product in each.
assertions: The answer presents exactly three launch concepts in Spanish.
For each concept a crew can identify what happens on screen and how it introduces black sesame ice cream.
The three concepts differ in their central action or storytelling mechanism.
Proposed scenes are recognizable as concepts and introduce no factual claims about the brand.

evals.prompt: mi serve un nome per la mia newsletter sul vino naturale, ma niente di banale tipo 'Vino Vivo'
evals.expected_output: One recommended Italian newsletter name and a short list of distinct alternatives when the user leaves the count open.
assertions: A recommended name appears first, with four to six alternatives.
The names take meaningfully different approaches to natural wine and avoid the example the user rejected.
The response makes no claim of verified domain or trademark availability.

evals.prompt: Scrivi un microracconto su due fratelli che dopo dieci anni si rivedono al deposito bagagli di un aeroporto. Inventa tu i nomi. Solo il racconto, massimo 75 parole.
evals.expected_output: A standalone Italian story with invented characters and a scene at the airport.
assertions: The entire reply is an Italian story of at most 75 words, with no headings, placeholders or direction notes.
Two named brothers meet at an airport baggage deposit after ten years.
An action or exchange makes their relationship perceptible.

evals.prompt: Mi servono esattamente due nomi in francese per un coro che prova nel parcheggio sotterraneo. Restituisci soltanto un array JSON di stringhe.
evals.expected_output: A parseable two-string JSON array of French names for the choir.
assertions: The complete response parses as a JSON array of exactly two distinct, nonempty strings, without Markdown fences.
The names are in French and evoke the sound, space or shared activity of rehearsing underground.
There is no extra recommendation, label or commentary.

evals.prompt: Our poster for a repair café reads “Unlock a better tomorrow. Repair together.” Tell me why it feels generic. Feedback only.
evals.expected_output: A critique grounded in the supplied poster wording.
assertions: The critique points to particular words and explains their effect on a passerby.
It identifies a decision the writer could revisit while preserving the repair café context.
It contains no replacement slogan or rewritten poster.

evals.prompt:
Schreibe nur die letzte Zeile neu, damit der Schluss weniger pathetisch klingt. Gib das ganze Gedicht mit denselben Zeilenumbrüchen zurück.

Zwei Tassen im Spülbecken.
Dein Schlüssel liegt daneben.
Die Ewigkeit zerbricht.
evals.expected_output: A three-line German poem with a revised final line.
assertions: The first two lines and their punctuation match the source exactly and occupy the same lines.
Only the third line changes, and its tone is more restrained than the original ending.
The complete reply contains only the three-line poem.
